dedupe_keys.name: xeoverse real time leo mega constellation network simulator on mininet

description: xeoverse is a network simulator for research on LEO satellite networks, built because testing on real mega-constellations is expensive or impossible while some are not yet deployed. It models user terminals, satellites and ground stations as lightweight Linux virtual machines inside Mininet and uses three strategies, pre-computing topology and routing changes, updating only the inter-satellite links that change, and keeping only the links relevant to the scenario, to run in real time, where one simulated second equals one wall-clock second; the authors report that it outperforms state-of-the-art simulators. Producer: Kassem and Sastry; the arXiv preprint was first submitted on 17 June 2024. Coverage: generic LEO mega-constellations, worldwide. Access: the abstract page gives the paper only; whether the code can be downloaded was not confirmed, so open_source is recorded as false, meaning no verified open-source release. Licence and cost: not stated for the software; the paper is free and it is under the CC-BY-4.0. Caveats: results come from the paper's evaluations, and how well the pre-computed routing represents operator networks was not assessed here. Simulation uses: it supports capacity planning, protocol testing and end-to-end traffic experiments on constellations such as Starlink-scale networks. Related records: OpenSN (platform-opensn), the Hypatia simulator (model-hypatia) and Mininet-Optical (platform-mininet-optical).
